key_insight: WEST is a scalable open-source platform that enables large-scale excited-state simulations by combining GW, Bethe-Salpeter, TDDFT, and embedding methods without explicit virtual states.
engineering_relevance: For perovskite solar cells, WEST can model optical response, self-trapped excitons, and excited-state processes at realistic system sizes, supporting materials design and device-relevant prediction.
method: Full-frequency GW, Bethe-Salpeter equation, and TDDFT in one framework
Avoids explicit virtual-state sums using density functional and density matrix perturbation theory
Uses low-rank screening/exact-exchange representations, localization, and GPU-parallel scaling
evidence_signal: The abstract reports near-ideal strong scaling to thousands of GPUs and successful applications to systems with more than a thousand atoms, including self-trapped excitons in metal-halide perovskites.
watch_item: Performance and accuracy depend on complex HPC/GPU workflows and advanced approximations, which may increase implementation and reproducibility overhead.
paper_title: The WEST code for large-scale excited-state materials simulations
